articles.title: Newsmax Fears Fox Freeze-Out on Roku if Merger Is Not Blocked
articles.summary: Newsmax filed an antitrust lawsuit on Thursday that seeks to block the Fox-Roku merger, arguing that the deal gives Fox unlawful monopoly power over the free streaming market. Fox Corp. closed the $22 billion acquisition earlier this month.
body: But in its lawsuit, Newsmax alleges that those commitments are unenforceable, and raises fears that Fox will deprive it of a key distribution channel.

“No single media company should have the power to determine which news voices Americans can see or hear,” said Christopher Ruddy, the CEO of Newsmax, in a statement. “Fox already dominates cable news and has repeatedly sought to undermine Newsmax as a competitor. Now Fox wants to control the very platforms and technology that millions of Americans use to access news and information.”
According to the complaint, Fox will control some 70% of the free, ad-supported streaming TV market through its ownership of Roku and Tubi.

“Fox has a long history of anticompetitive animus toward Newsmax,” the lawsuit states. “Most notably, Fox has refused to carry Newsmax on Fox’s own free streaming service, Tubi. Now that Fox has acquired Roku – along with (the Roku Channel) – the risk that Fox will further degrade distribution of Newsmax’s content is clear.”

articles.title: Guarding Stars review – Leighton Meester is a delight in fizzy Netflix holiday romance
articles.summary: As a female bodyguard protecting an A-list star, the Gossip Girl actor shines in Christmas movie a cut above the competition. Though it is my personal opinion that Christmas should not begin until after Thanksgiving, I am pleased to say that we already have at least one treat in Netflix’s holiday…
body: Good holiday movies are an exercise in knowing silliness, and so it is a relief when the first 10 minutes of this movie, directed by Elizabeth Allen Rosenbaum, strikes the rare December balance between hearth-like warmth (the twinkle in Meester’s chocolate eyes when her Hannah Brooks lands a verbal punch) and complete lunacy (she lands that punch in an argument with her ex about … cuddling … literally seconds after thwarting an assassination attempt in Times Square). As a homespun band of hot would-be cowboys later drawl at a Christmas parade in “Montana” (Canada, per usual): “Christmas is back, y’all.”

So is Meester: the actor still best known for playing the Upper East Side’s ultimate ice queen in Gossip Girl is one of the few who can pull off “career woman with a heart of stone” with enough zest to overpower cliche. One believes, even accepts, when Meester’s Hannah, dressed in FBI office drag and glasses almost campy in their unsexiness, refuses both hugs and the suggestion of paid rest following the death of her mother, instead opting for the assignment in Montana because she feels “constantly overlooked and underestimated, nobody sees me coming”.

articles.title: Taylor Swift Performs ‘I Knew It, I Knew You’ and ‘Our Song’ Mashup at CMA Awards
articles.summary: “It’s been a while,” Taylor Swift sang during her performance of “I Knew It, I Knew You” at the Country Music Association Awards on Wednesday night — and it sure was, marking her first time performing at the show in 13 years. The singer gave the first public performance of “I Knew It, I Knew
body: It was a welcome return to the CMA stage for Swift, who performed at the ceremony back in 2013 when she received the Pinnacle Award and sang “Red” with Vince Gill and Alison Krauss. She last appeared at the CMAs in 2016 as a surprise presenter to give Entertainer of the Year to Garth Brooks.

Her cameo at the show comes 20 years after her first appearance at the CMAs. Swift recently made a foray back into country with her “Toy Story 5” single “I Knew It, I Knew You,” which was her first new song in over a decade to be marketed as a country song. She made a bold pivot to pop back in 2015 when she released “1989,” though she had experimented with pop and dubstep on her smash album “Red” on songs like “We Are Never Getting Back Together” and “22.”

Swift is nominated at the CMAs this year with “I Knew It, I Knew You,” which is up for single of the year. Earlier this week, she picked up five Grammy nominations, including album of the year for “The Life of a Showgirl”; song of the year and best song written for visual media for “I Knew It, I Knew You”; best pop duo/group performance for “The Life of a Showgirl” with Sabrina Carpenter; and record of the year for “The Fate of Ophelia.”

articles.title: Ella Langley Wins Six Trophies at CMA Awards, Including Entertainer of the Year: The Complete List of Winners
articles.summary: In a near-sweep that surprised no one, Ella Langley won six trophies at the CMA Awards, including the top prize, entertainer of the year. The “Choosin’ Texas” singer so swept the field that the show’s host, Lainey Wilson, came out with a broom during her final acceptance speech and pretended to be…
body: Ella Langley won nearly every award she was up for, including the top prize, as well as female vocalist and album, single and song of the year. Stephen Wilson Jr. was a surprise to many in being named best new artist. Taylor Swift sang her nominated song and presented a lifetime achievement award to Brooks & Dunn.

“I watched these awards since i was a little kid, and the awards i cared most about were song of the year and entertainer of the year,” Langley said at the close. Ultimately, after five turns at the podium (the sixth award was announced pre-telecast), she said, “I’ve run out of things to say. I’m at a loss for words.” But, she finally added, “I could quit tomorrow and have the best year of my life.”

Among the early wins was an upset, but not a complete shock to industry insiders — a win for Stephen Wilson Jr. as new artist of the year. Wilson thanked his wife, Sixpence None the Richer singer Leigh Nash, among others. Noting just how unusual his career course had been, Wilson said, “I left my job as a scientist. I’d never sung a song in my life for anybody. A lot can happen in 12 years.”

“As Jason pointed out, it really still is Blumhouse movies and Atomic Monster movies,” Wan added. “We’re still making the movies as one company, but still under two labels. articles.title: Madden review – Nicolas Cage is a cartoonish NFL legend in David O Russell’s stinker
articles.summary: Oscar-nominated director delivers a thoroughly unserious biopic, wasting Christian Bale and Sienna Miller’s talents. John Madden was a beloved American original, the burly football coach who segued easily from Super Bowl burnout to television darling to the last name in gaming as the NFL was…
body: That the Madden video game franchise outlived the avuncular Minnesotan, whose death at age 85 in 2021 was mourned throughout the sport, is as much a testament to his singular knack for teaching the game’s fundaments as it is to his willingness to bring his classroom to students, wherever they might huddle. But Madden, a new Amazon biopic that can’t decide whether it’s serious or slapstick, has drawn all the wrong lessons.

Mulaney knows the film he’s in is a stinker – and so, for that matter, does Miller. She looks like she might crack up at the ridiculousness in early scenes as Raiders first lady Carol Davis. But in her defense: it would be hard for anyone to keep a straight face opposite Bale – who more than justifies the makeup and costuming departments’ considerable efforts to revive Davis, the NFL’s immortal rogue. Bale nails Davis’s Brooklyn accent, the pimp swagger and his roiling insistence on being the smartest guy in the room – right down to diagnosing Madden’s persistent stomach problems as “gas”. Turns out, it was a bleeding ulcer.

articles.title: Zombucha! review – new Australian zombie film never quite finds its bite
articles.summary: An accident in kombucha brewing leads to a zombie outbreak in a movie which is a little too low-key to live up to its delicious potential. Get our weekend culture and lifestyle email. Zombucha! is a relatively rare example of a genre film that’s not really a genre film.
body: What we do get is an enjoyably staged and well-paced production that’s never boring, despite the long wait for the main action. There’s also something kind of endearing about a zombie film so low-key it almost forgets to be a zombie film. Emma Leonard’s writing, Claudia Dzienny’s direction and the performances are all appealing, albeit lacking some flair. I was consistently entertained but will probably never return for a rewatch.

Meanwhile, her husband, Leo (Ryan O’Kane), the creative director at an advertising agency, is getting great feedback from clients – his ad for an energy drink considered “poetic” and “paradigm-shifting”. But he’s tired of working crazy long hours for the “toxic capitalist machine”, despite some generous perks from his boss Hopper (Jackie van Beek), such as a bag of white powder to help him power through. So Leo quits his job, which Maddie isn’t thrilled about, given she lost hers on the same day and the pair are “mortgaged up to the freakin’ eyeballs”.

articles.title: Hunger Games fan, 13, to get artwork shown on cinema screens before film
articles.summary: Freja Brown beat more than 1,000 entries and met some of the stars after winning a competition.
body: A teenage Hunger Games fan has met the cast of the new film after her artwork won a competition, meaning it will be displayed at every cinema screening across the UK.

Freja Brown, 13, won the British Board of Film Classification's (BBFC) create the card competition, which ran ahead of the release of The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping - the sixth film in the franchise.
Freja, from Cardiff, beat more than 1,000 entries from across the UK and said she was "so grateful" to be chosen.
Her design will be the official BBFC black card, which displays the age rating and classification details of the film before every cinema showing.

articles.title: Josephine review – Channing Tatum and Gemma Chan ballast knotty drama about a child witness to a rape
articles.summary: Mason Reeves steals the show as an eight year old who stumbles across a sex assault but, despite strong performances, parts of the film feel contrived. Beth de Araújo’s new movie takes a very big swing, and it has won prizes and acclaim since its premiere at Sundance.
body: Channing Tatum and Gemma Chan play Damien and Claire, a smart professional couple in San Francisco with a bright young daughter called Josephine, marvellously played by Reeves. Damien takes Josephine to Golden Gate Park one morning to play football (they turn out to enjoy watching the English Premier League on TV). She mischievously runs on ahead of her dad to a secluded spot in the park where Damien can’t immediately find her and it is there that Josephine witnesses a rape – not less horrifying for being filmed in long shot.

Damien catches up with Josephine, and gives chase to the rapist; Josephine and the rape victim find themselves in the back of a police car while the cops and Damien deal with matters, almost as if they are culprits and prisoners. Deeply affected by something she cannot understand or process in her mind, Josephine starts acting out in school, not helped by Damien bizarrely insisting she take self-defence classes. Her disorientation borders on psychosis, and all the time the court date nears when Josephine has to give evidence in front of a jury.
points: Mason Reeves steals the show as an eight year old who stumbles across a sex assault but, despite strong performances, parts of the film feel contrived.
Beth de Araújo’s new movie takes a very big swing, and it has won prizes and acclaim since its premiere at Sundance.

articles.title: Grand Theft Auto 6 is a masterpiece, say critics
articles.summary: Critics have their say as to whether GTA 6, the most anticipated video game of all time, lives up to the hype.
body: After 13 years of waiting, record-breaking trailers and lengthy delays, critics have given their answer to one of the year's biggest questions.
Does Grand Theft Auto 6, surely the most anticipated game of all time, live up to the hype?
Metacritic, which aggregates reviews from critics, averages it at 99 out of 100, external - tying with Nintendo's The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, which has held the record since 1998.
Reviewers overwhelmingly agreed the open-world action game was an ambitious, ground-breaking title that was well worth the wait.

articles.title: ‘Secret Lives of Mormon Wives’ EPs on How ‘Orange County’ Became the First Franchise Extension, Season 2 Hopes and “Exploring” More Spinoffs
articles.summary: Jeff Jenkins and Lisa Filipelli speak with THR about expanding the ‘Mormon Wives’ franchise, what spinoffs they hope to pursue in the future and how the cast set OC's first season up for success.
body: Hulu ’s first extension of The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives franchise arrived on the streamer last Thursday, introducing viewers to a brand-new pool of women based in Southern California who are in some way connected to the LDS faith.
So, what actually is in the secret sauce in Hulu’s The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives format? Executive producers Jeff Jenkins and Lisa Filipelli both agree everything boils down to casting.

“A docuseries, in my opinion, is only as good as the folks who are the subject, who are on camera, right? So we just try really hard to collaborate with our cast members and bring their stories forward,” Jenkins says. “It just goes back to story and sharing. We look for subjects, castmembers, who are really ready to share. It’s not an easy thing to do.”

Most of the women, like the original show, have built a presence on social media before reality television cameras began capturing their lives. Among them are Aspyn Ovard, an original family channel YouTuber who is now in a throuple; Madison Bontempo, another family-style YouTuber who used to be close with the Paul brothers; and Bobbi Althoff, the podcaster behind those viral Drake and Lil Yachty interviews.
